0: Case Closed by Gosho Aoyama (Viz Media) is a lighthearted mystery series with a new puzzle around every corner. Teen detective Jimmy Kudo stumbles onto a shady deal, and the criminals force a strange poison on him that shrinks him into a little kid. Hiding under the name Conan Edogawa, he keeps solving cases in secret while hunting the organization that did this to him. It suits readers who love clever whodunits.
1: Ranma 1/2 by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a madcap martial arts comedy with a romantic streak. Teenage fighter Ranma Saotome fell into a cursed spring in China, and now cold water turns him into a girl while hot water changes him back. His father has also promised him in marriage to Akane Tendo, a tough girl who wants nothing to do with him. Expect slapstick brawls, rivals, and plenty of mixed-up hearts.
2: Hayate the Combat Butler by Kenjiro Hata (Viz Media) is a goofy romantic comedy packed with anime and pop culture jokes. Sixteen-year-old Hayate Ayasaki learns his deadbeat parents have sold him off to cover their gambling debts. A desperate plan goes sideways, and he ends up working as a butler for Nagi Sanzenin, a wealthy, sheltered girl. It is a fun pick for readers who like over-the-top gags and sweet moments.
3: Kingdom Hearts by Shiro Amano (Tokyopop) is a bright, kid-friendly adventure based on the video game. Sora is a boy living on a quiet island with his friends Riku and Kairi, until a dark storm tears their world apart. He wakes up holding the Keyblade and teams up with Donald Duck and Goofy to search for his missing friends. Fans of the game and of Disney characters will feel right at home.
4: The Prince of Tennis by Takeshi Konomi (Viz Media) is an energetic sports series about a young tennis prodigy. Ryoma Echizen comes back from winning junior tournaments in America and joins the tennis club at Seishun Academy. He is only a first-year, but his skill and cocky attitude soon have the upperclassmen paying attention. It is a great pick for readers who enjoy rivalries, big matches, and showy special moves.
5: Toriko by Mitsutoshi Shimabukuro (Viz Media) is a big-hearted action adventure about food. In a world where the finest ingredients are found in dangerous wild lands, Toriko is a Gourmet Hunter who tracks down rare and tasty beasts. A timid hotel chef named Komatsu tags along, hoping to see legendary ingredients for himself. Expect giant monsters, huge appetites, and a story that is always ready for the next meal.
6: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure by Hirohiko Araki (Viz Media) is a stylish, strange action saga that follows the Joestar family across generations. It begins in Victorian England, where young Jonathan Joestar's life is turned upside down when his father adopts the cunning Dio Brando. An ancient stone mask soon pulls them into a fight against forces far beyond ordinary. Readers who love bold art, odd powers, and dramatic poses will enjoy it.
7: Flame of Recca by Nobuyuki Anzai (Viz Media) is a fiery action series with a ninja-loving hero. High schooler Recca Hanabishi dreams of being a ninja and can somehow create flames with his hands. When he meets Yanagi Sakoshita, a gentle girl with the power to heal, he swears to protect her as her ninja. Their bond pulls them into a world of tournament battles and magical weapons.
8: Boys Over Flowers by Yoko Kamio (Viz Media) is a classic high school romance with plenty of drama. Tsukushi Makino is a working-class girl at an elite academy ruled by the F4, four rich boys who bully anyone they dislike. When Tsukushi stands up for a friend, she becomes their next target, but she refuses to back down. Readers who like spirited heroines and stormy love stories will enjoy it.
9: Kekkaishi by Yellow Tanabe (Viz Media) is a supernatural action series with a touch of comedy. Yoshimori Sumimura is a teen barrier master whose family has guarded a special piece of land for generations. By day it is his school, and by night he fights demons there alongside Tokine, the girl next door from a rival family. It is a solid pick for fans of monster-fighting adventures.
10: Land of the Lustrous by Haruko Ichikawa (Kodansha) is a beautiful, melancholy fantasy. Far in the future, living gem people called Lustrous defend themselves against the Lunarians, who come from the moon to shatter and steal them. Phosphophyllite is the youngest and most fragile gem, too brittle to fight; assigned to write an encyclopedia, Phos sets out to find a real purpose. It suits readers who like quiet, thoughtful stories with striking art.
12: Vagabond by Takehiko Inoue (Viz Media) is a sweeping historical drama about Japan's most famous swordsman. After the battle of Sekigahara, a wild young man named Takezo returns home as a hunted outcast. He takes the name Miyamoto Musashi and sets out on a path of duels, hoping to become the strongest swordsman of all. With gorgeous brushwork and deep characters, it rewards readers who like serious, grounded stories.
14: Kaze Hikaru by Taeko Watanabe (Viz Media) is a historical drama with a quiet romance at its heart. In 1863 Kyoto, a girl named Tominaga Sei disguises herself as a boy to join the Mibu-roshi, the samurai band that would become the Shinsengumi. She hopes to avenge her murdered father and brother. Hiding her secret while training alongside the warriors, she grows close to the kind captain Okita Soji.
15: Trinity Seven by Kenji Saito (Yen Press) is a magical school action comedy with plenty of fan service. Arata Kasuga's ordinary life ends when a strange event swallows his town and his cousin Hijiri disappears. Hoping to find her, he enrolls at the Royal Biblia Academy, a school for mages. There he meets the Trinity Seven, seven powerful girls who each master a different kind of magic.
16: Rave Master by Hiro Mashima (Tokyopop) is a cheerful fantasy adventure from the creator of Fairy Tail. Haru Glory lives a quiet life on a small island until he meets Plue, an odd little creature, and learns he is chosen to wield the holy stones called Rave. With a giant sword in hand, he sets out to stop an evil group using the dark stones. Fans of friendship-driven quests will feel right at home.
17: Natsume's Book of Friends by Yuki Midorikawa (Viz Media) is a gentle supernatural story with a warm heart. Takashi Natsume has always been able to see yokai, the spirits most people cannot. After he inherits his late grandmother's Book of Friends, a book holding the names of spirits she bound, the yokai start coming for him; with a cat-shaped spirit as his bodyguard, he decides to return their names. It is a soothing, tender read.
18: Dragon Knights by Mineko Ohkami (Tokyopop) is a lively fantasy adventure with plenty of humor. Rath, Thatz, and Rune are three very different dragon knights who serve the Dragon Lord of Dragonia. Rath is a hotheaded fighter, Thatz is a greedy treasure lover, and Rune is a gentle elf. Their missions against demons send them across the land in a mix of magic, swordplay, and banter.
19: Excel Saga by Rikdo Koshi (Viz Media) is a wacky, anything-goes comedy. Excel is a hyperactive young woman fiercely loyal to Il Palazzo, the leader of a secret group called ACROSS that plans to take over the world one city at a time. Along with her fragile partner Hyatt, she bumbles through missions while trying to survive her day jobs. Readers who enjoy chaotic gags and parody will have a blast.
20: Slam Dunk by Takehiko Inoue (Viz Media) is a beloved basketball story with big laughs and real heart. Hanamichi Sakuragi is a tall, hot-tempered delinquent who has been rejected by fifty girls. When the cute Haruko Akagi asks if he likes basketball, he joins the team to impress her, even though he has never played. It is a great pick for sports fans and anyone who likes an underdog.
21: In Another World With My Smartphone by Patora Fuyuhara (J-Novel Club) is a relaxed, easygoing fantasy comedy. Touya Mochizuki is killed by a god's mistake, and the apologetic deity lets him be reborn in a fantasy world. As a bonus, Touya brings his smartphone, which still works there; with a knack for every kind of magic, he sets off on a laid-back journey and makes plenty of friends. It suits readers who want a breezy, cheerful isekai.
22: Oresama Teacher by Izumi Tsubaki (Viz Media) is a high-energy school comedy. Mafuyu Kurosaki was the toughest delinquent at her old school, so after getting expelled, she is sent to a new one and swears to become a normal girl. Then she discovers her homeroom teacher is Takaomi, her childhood friend, who has his own plans for her. Fans of slapstick humor and tough heroines will love it.
23: Triage X by Shouji Sato (Yen Press) is a stylish action series with lots of fan service. On the surface, Mochizuki General Hospital is an ordinary place, but it secretly runs Black Label, a squad of vigilantes who remove the cancers of society. High schooler Arashi Mikami is one of its agents, taking on criminals the law cannot touch. Expect explosive gunfights and over-the-top action, best for older teens and adults.
24: Kimi ni Todoke by Karuho Shiina (Viz Media) is a sweet, gentle high school romance. Sawako Kuronuma is kind and earnest, but classmates nicknamed her Sadako after a horror movie ghost and keep their distance. Everything begins to change when Shota Kazehaya, the friendliest boy in class, starts talking to her. Readers who enjoy slow, heartfelt love stories and growing friendships will treasure it.
25: GetBackers by Yuya Aoki and Rando Ayamine (Tokyopop) is an action comedy about two unusual retrieval agents. Ban Mido and Ginji Amano run the GetBackers, a business that promises to get back anything that has been lost or stolen, for a price. Ban has a cursed evil eye, and Ginji can shoot electricity; their jobs drag them into the dangerous underworld of Tokyo. Fans of buddy action and strange powers will enjoy it.
26: InuYasha Ani-Manga by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) retells the anime in comic form using images from the show. Kagome Higurashi is a modern schoolgirl who falls down an old well at her family's shrine and lands in feudal Japan. There she frees InuYasha, a half-demon boy, and the two are forced to team up after a sacred jewel shatters. It is a great fit for fans of the show and classic adventure romance.
27: Chronicles of the Cursed Sword by Yeo Beop-Ryong (Tokyopop) is a Korean martial arts fantasy full of sword fights. Rey Yan is an orphan who carries the PaSa Sword, a demon blade that grants great power at a steep cost. With his friend Sharak by his side, he is drawn into a war between kingdoms and demons. Readers who like classic action and magical weapons will find plenty to enjoy.
28: Welcome to Demon School! Iruma-kun by Osamu Nishi (Kodansha) is a cheerful fantasy comedy. Fourteen-year-old Iruma Suzuki is sold to a demon by his careless parents; luckily, that demon is Sullivan, a kindly grandfather type who adopts him and enrolls him in a school for demons. Iruma has to hide that he is human while making friends among the strangest classmates around. It is a fun, feel-good read.
29: My Isekai Life by Shinkoshoto (Square Enix) is a cozy fantasy adventure. Yuji is an overworked office worker who suddenly finds himself in another world with the abilities of a Tamer and a Sage. He quickly befriends a group of cute slimes who help him with almost everything; Yuji simply wants a peaceful life, but his powers keep pulling him into bigger events. It suits readers who enjoy relaxed isekai stories.
30: Claymore by Norihiro Yagi (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy action series. In a world plagued by Yoma, shape-shifting monsters that feed on humans, villages hire half-human female warriors called Claymores to hunt them. Clare is one of these silver-eyed fighters; after she saves a boy named Raki, he begins to follow her on her journey. Readers who like grim fantasy and intense sword battles will be hooked.
31: Dr. Stone by Riichiro Inagaki and Boichi (Viz Media) is a sci-fi adventure about the power of science. A mysterious flash turns every human on Earth to stone; thousands of years later, a science-loving teen named Senku Ishigami breaks free and finds the world reclaimed by nature. Along with his strong but simple friend Taiju, he sets out to rebuild civilization from scratch. It is clever, upbeat, and full of hands-on experiments.
32: The Rising of the Shield Hero: The Manga Companion by Aneko Yusagi (One Peace Books) adapts the popular fantasy series. Naofumi Iwatani is a college student summoned to another world as one of four legendary heroes, but he gets the shield, the weakest weapon. Soon after, he is falsely accused and betrayed, leaving him alone and scorned; he has to build his strength from nothing. It suits readers who like gritty underdog fantasy.
33: Btooom! by Junya Inoue (Yen Press) is a tense survival thriller. Ryota Sakamoto is an unemployed gamer who is one of the top players of an online bomb-fighting game. One day he wakes up on a remote island and realizes he has been dropped into a real-life version of the game, with real bombs; to survive, he has to figure out who to trust. It is a fit for readers who like high-stakes action.
34: Snow White with the Red Hair by Sorata Akizuki (Viz Media) is a gentle fantasy romance. Shirayuki is a herbalist whose rare apple-red hair catches the eye of a spoiled prince who wants her as his concubine. She cuts her hair and flees to the neighboring kingdom, where she meets Zen, its kind second prince; with his help, she starts a new life as a court herbalist. It is a calm, warm-hearted read.
35: Soul Eater by Atsushi Ohkubo (Yen Press) is a stylish supernatural action series. At Death Weapon Meister Academy, students train in pairs, with one partner able to transform into a weapon. Maka Albarn and her partner Soul, who becomes a scythe, aim to collect the souls of 99 evil humans and one witch; doing so will make Soul a Death Scythe. It mixes quirky humor, spooky art, and lots of action.
36: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation by Rifujin na Magonote (Seven Seas) is a sweeping fantasy that helped shape the isekai genre. A jobless, regret-filled man dies and is reborn as Rudeus Greyrat, a baby in a world of magic. Keeping his old memories, he resolves to live this new life to the fullest. It follows his childhood and long journey in rich detail, best for older teens and adults.
37: Death March to the Parallel World Rhapsody by Hiro Ainana (Yen Press) is a breezy fantasy adventure. Overworked game programmer Ichiro Suzuki falls asleep after a long stretch at work and wakes up in a world that looks a lot like the games he builds. Thanks to a powerful spell he uses right away, he finds himself at an incredibly high level; taking the name Satou, he sets off sightseeing. It is a relaxed, easygoing read.
38: Yakitate!! Japan by Takashi Hashiguchi (Viz Media) is a high-energy comedy about baking. Kazuma Azuma has unusually warm hands, perfect for making bread, and he dreams of creating a national bread for Japan that can rival French and German loaves. He heads to Tokyo to join a famous bakery chain and test his skills against other bakers. Expect wild reactions, food puns, and a surprising amount of real baking.
39: Dragon Ball by Akira Toriyama (Viz Media) is the classic adventure that started a legend. Goku is a monkey-tailed boy with super strength who lives alone in the mountains; when a clever girl named Bulma shows up hunting for the seven Dragon Balls, which can grant any wish, he joins her quest. Their journey leads to martial arts tournaments, colorful friends, and tougher foes. It is fun, funny, and full of heart.
40: Mao by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery from the creator of InuYasha. Years ago, middle schooler Nanoka Kiba survived an accident that killed her parents. One day, walking through an old shopping arcade, she finds herself in the Taisho era, where she meets Mao, a young exorcist; he believes she may hold the key to his own curse. Fans of eerie folklore and slow-burn mysteries will enjoy it.
41: Accel World by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series from the creator of Sword Art Online. Haruyuki Arita is a short, bullied boy who escapes into virtual games at school. Everything changes when Kuroyukihime, the school's beautiful vice president, gives him a program called Brain Burst, which speeds up thought itself; with it, he enters a hidden fighting game. It is a fit for readers who like virtual-world battles.
42: Astro Boy by Osamu Tezuka (Dark Horse) is the classic sci-fi series from the godfather of manga. After his son dies, the brilliant scientist Dr. Tenma builds a robot boy in his image; the robot, Astro, has amazing powers and a kind heart. Each story explores what it means to be human as Astro protects people and robots alike. It is a timeless pick for kids and longtime fans.
43: Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan by Hiroshi Shiibashi (Viz Media) is a supernatural action series. Rikuo Nura is a seemingly normal middle schooler, but he is also one-quarter yokai and grandson of the leader of a powerful yokai clan. By day he wants nothing to do with that world, but by night his yokai side awakens. It suits readers who enjoy Japanese folklore, monster battles, and coming-of-age stories.
44: Kamisama Kiss by Julietta Suzuki (Viz Media) is a charming supernatural romance. High schooler Nanami Momozono is left homeless after her father skips town on his gambling debts. A stranger she helps gives her his home, which turns out to be a shrine, and his job as its local god; now she has to learn to be a deity, with the help of a grumpy fox spirit named Tomoe. It is sweet and funny.
45: Rebirth by Woo (Tokyopop) is a dark action fantasy from Korea. Deshwitat is a vampire who was sealed away for three hundred years after being betrayed by Kalutika, a sorcerer who murdered the woman he loved. When the seal is finally broken, he wakes in a changed world with only one goal, revenge. Readers who like brooding heroes, gothic atmosphere, and big battles will find a lot to enjoy here.
46: Yu-Gi-Oh! Duelist by Kazuki Takahashi (Viz Media) is a card-battle adventure; Yugi Mutou is a shy boy who loves games, and solving the ancient Millennium Puzzle awakened a bold spirit inside him. In these volumes, Yugi heads to an island tournament after a powerful game designer kidnaps his grandfather's soul; to win him back, he must take on top duelists. Fans of strategy and card games will enjoy every duel.
47: Zatch Bell! by Makoto Raiku (Viz Media) is a heartfelt action comedy. Kiyo Takamine is a gloomy genius who has no friends until his father sends him Zatch, a little boy with no memories. Zatch is one of a hundred mamodo children fighting to become the next king of their world, and with Kiyo reading spells from his book, Zatch can shoot lightning. It is a great mix of laughs and battles.
48: A Certain Magical Index by Kazuma Kamachi (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action series where science and magic collide. Toma Kamijo lives in Academy City, where students develop psychic powers; his right hand can cancel any supernatural power, but it also seems to cancel his luck. One day he finds a young nun named Index hanging over his balcony, and she is being chased by magicians. It is a fit for readers who like big casts and battles.
49: GTO: Great Teacher Onizuka by Tohru Fujisawa (Tokyopop) is a rowdy comedy with a big heart. Eikichi Onizuka is a 22-year-old former gang member with no real qualifications, but he decides he wants to become a teacher. He lands a job at a private school and takes charge of a class that has driven other teachers away. His unorthodox methods make for laughs and surprisingly moving moments.
50: Hoshin Engi by Ryu Fujisaki (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure inspired by an old Chinese legend. Taikobo is a laid-back trainee immortal who is given a huge task: capture hundreds of evil spirits that have been causing chaos in the human world. Many of them serve Dakki, a fox spirit who has charmed the king of the Yin dynasty. Fans of clever heroes and wild magical battles will enjoy it.
51: Infinite Dendrogram by Sakon Kaidou (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy adventure set inside a groundbreaking virtual reality game. College student Reiji Mukudori finally starts playing Infinite Dendrogram, a game said to offer endless possibilities, with his older brother. When his player companion, called an Embryo, hatches, it turns out to be a girl named Nemesis; Reiji soon learns this game world feels very real. It suits fans of game-world stories.
52: Chibi Vampire by Yuna Kagesaki (Tokyopop) is a sweet and silly supernatural romantic comedy. Karin Maaka comes from a family of vampires, but she is the odd one out; instead of drinking blood, she produces too much of it, and if she does not give it away, she gets terrible nosebleeds. Things get tricky when the new boy at school seems to make her blood rush. It is lighthearted fun.
53: Sakamoto Days by Yuto Suzuki (Viz Media) is an action comedy about a hitman who retired for love. Taro Sakamoto was once the greatest assassin of all, until he fell in love, got married, and quit. Now he is a chubby, quiet convenience store owner with a wife and daughter; when a big bounty is placed on his head, old enemies come calling. Expect creative fights and a lot of laughs.
54: Whistle! by Daisuke Higuchi (Viz Media) is an underdog sports story about soccer. Sho Kazamatsuri loves the game, but he is so small that he never made it off the bench at his old powerhouse school. He transfers to Josui Junior High hoping for a fresh start and a real chance to play. It is a heartfelt pick for readers who enjoy hard work, teamwork, and growing friendships.
55: Servamp by Strike Tanaka (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action series about vampires and their partners. High schooler Mahiru Shirota prefers simple, easy choices, so when he finds a stray black cat, he takes it home and names it Kuro. Kuro is actually a lazy vampire, one of seven powerful servamps; by naming him, Mahiru becomes his partner and is drawn into a war among vampires. It is a good fit for fans of moody action.
56: Spice and Wolf by Isuna Hasekura (Yen Press) is a thoughtful fantasy about trade, travel, and companionship. Kraft Lawrence is a traveling merchant who finds a surprise in his wagon: Holo, a wolf goddess of the harvest in the form of a young woman. Holo wants to return to her northern home, so the two travel together. It is a rich, slow-paced story full of witty banter and business deals.
57: Wind Breaker by Satoru Nii (Kodansha) is a delinquent action series with heart. Haruka Sakura is a loner who only trusts his fists, and he enrolls at Furin High School to fight his way to the top. He learns that the school's students are tough fighters who use their strength to protect their town. Readers who like street fights, loyalty, and friendship will be pulled right in.
58: 20th Century Boys by Naoki Urasawa (Viz Media) is a gripping mystery thriller. Kenji Endo runs a convenience store and has put aside his childhood dreams; then a mysterious cult leader known as Friend begins using a symbol that Kenji and his friends made up as kids. As strange events unfold, Kenji has to reunite his old friends and remember what they once imagined. It is perfect for readers who love twisty, layered plots.
59: Gintama by Hideaki Sorachi (Viz Media) is a gag-packed action comedy set in an alternate Edo. Aliens have taken over Japan and banned swords, but Gintoki Sakata still carries a wooden one. He runs an odd jobs business, taking any work that pays the rent; with his teen helper Shinpachi and the alien girl Kagura, he gets into all kinds of trouble. It is great for fans of parody and sudden serious turns.
60: Terra Formars by Yu Sasuga (Viz Media) is a brutal sci-fi action series. Centuries ago, humans sent cockroaches to Mars to help make the planet livable; now a crew is sent to clear the pests, only to find they have evolved into huge, humanlike creatures. To fight back, the crew has been given the abilities of different insects and animals. It is intense and violent, best for older readers who like survival stories.
61: My Monster Secret by Eiji Masuda (Seven Seas) is a silly school romantic comedy. Asahi Kuromine is a high school boy who has never been able to keep a secret; when he finally works up the nerve to confess to his crush, Youko Shiragami, he discovers that she is actually a vampire. Now he has to protect her secret, and soon other classmates with secrets show up. It is light, sweet, and funny.
62: The Elusive Samurai by Yusei Matsui (Viz Media) is a historical action series from the creator of Assassination Classroom. In 1333, young Hojo Tokiyuki is the heir to Japan's ruling shogunate, until a trusted general betrays his family. Tokiyuki escapes with the help of an eccentric priest who sees that the boy has a gift for running and hiding. It mixes real history, humor, and lots of clever action.
63: The Ideal Sponger Life by Tsunehiko Watanabe (Seven Seas) is a laid-back fantasy comedy. Zenjirou is a hardworking office employee who dreams of an easy life; one day he is suddenly summoned to another world by Aura, a queen who wants him as her husband. If he agrees, he will never have to work again, though royal life comes with its own challenges. It suits readers who like relaxing isekai stories.
64: Ouran High School Host Club by Bisco Hatori (Viz Media) is a sparkling romantic comedy. Haruhi Fujioka is a scholarship student at a school for the super-rich; while looking for a quiet place to study, she stumbles into the host club and breaks an expensive vase. To pay off the debt, she has to work for the club, and since everyone thinks she is a boy, she becomes a host. It is funny and charming.
65: Itsuwaribito by Yuuki Iinuma (Viz Media) is an action adventure about a boy who lies to do good. Utsuho Nanase grew up as an orphan who loved to trick people; after a tragedy, he vows to become the greatest liar in the world, using his lies only to help others. He sets out on a journey through a land full of danger and dishonest people. It is great for fans of clever, scrappy heroes.
66: Kare Kano by Masami Tsuda (Tokyopop) is a thoughtful romantic comedy about putting on a front. Yukino Miyazawa is the perfect student, but it is all an act to win praise; at home, she is lazy and messy. Her plan is threatened when Soichiro Arima, a boy who seems even more perfect, starts at her school and discovers her secret. Their story looks honestly at love, family, and growing up.
67: Dorohedoro by Q Hayashida (Viz Media) is a gritty, darkly funny fantasy unlike anything else. In a grimy city called the Hole, sorcerers come from another world to test their magic on the people living there. Caiman is a man whose head was turned into a lizard by a sorcerer and who has no memory of who he was; with his friend Nikaido, he hunts sorcerers looking for answers. It is violent, best for older readers.
68: Yo-kai Watch by Noriyuki Konishi (Viz Media) is a goofy, kid-friendly comedy. Nate is an ordinary boy who opens a capsule toy machine and frees Whisper, a ghostly yo-kai. Whisper gives Nate a special watch that lets him see yo-kai, the spirits who cause everyday mischief; with help from friends like Jibanyan, Nate befriends and battles spirits. It is a fun read for young fans of the game and show.
69: Fairy Tail: 100 Years Quest by Hiro Mashima and Atsuo Ueda (Kodansha) is the official sequel to Fairy Tail. Natsu, Lucy, Happy, Gray, Erza, and Wendy decide to take on the 100 Years Quest, a mission so hard that no one has finished it in a century. It leads them to a new continent full of powerful foes. Fans of the original will be thrilled to rejoin their favorite guild.
70: Shangri-La Frontier by Katarina and Ryosuke Fuji (Kodansha) is a fast-paced fantasy action series. Rakuro Hizutome is a gamer who loves playing broken, glitchy games just to beat them. For a change, he decides to try Shangri-La Frontier, a polished VR game with millions of players; using the skills he learned from bad games, he quickly makes waves. It is great for fans of game-world stories and creative fights.
71: Sorcerer Hunters by Satoru Akahori and Ray Omishi (Tokyopop) is a zany fantasy action comedy. In a land where cruel sorcerers abuse ordinary people, a group of hunters is sent to stop them. Carrot Glace is a lovable goof with a strange curse that turns him into a monster, and sisters Tira and Chocolate Misu fight alongside him. Expect wild transformations, jokes, and over-the-top fantasy fun.
72: The Heroic Legend of Arslan by Yoshiki Tanaka and Hiromu Arakawa (Kodansha) is a sweeping historical fantasy. Arslan is the gentle young prince of Pars, a powerful kingdom. When an invading army overruns his homeland and his father's army falls, he must flee with a small band of loyal followers; Arslan has to find a way to retake his kingdom. It is a fit for readers who like war, strategy, and growing heroes.
73: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya by Nagaru Tanigawa (Yen Press) is a quirky school comedy with a sci-fi twist. Kyon is a regular high schooler who sits behind Haruhi Suzumiya, a girl who is only interested in aliens, time travelers, and espers. She drags him into forming the SOS Brigade to find them; what Haruhi does not know is that strange things are already happening around her. It is funny and clever.
74: Orient by Shinobu Ohtaka (Kodansha) is an action fantasy from the creator of Magi. Musashi grew up in a world where demons rule as gods and the samurai who once fought them are seen as villains. He dreams of becoming a samurai with his childhood friend Kojiro to free the land. It is a great pick for fans of shonen battles and found family.
75: Blue Box by Kouji Miura (Viz Media) is a gentle sports romance. Taiki Inomata is a member of his school's badminton team who has a crush on Chinatsu Kano, a star basketball player and an upperclassman. He thinks she is out of his league, until a family arrangement has her staying at his house; while both chase their sports goals, their bond quietly grows. It is a warm, heartfelt read.
76: The Devil Is a Part-Timer! by Satoshi Wagahara (Yen Press) is a fun fantasy comedy. The Devil King Satan was close to conquering his world when a hero drove him off, forcing him through a portal to modern Tokyo. With little magic left, he has to take a job at a fast-food restaurant to pay rent; then the hero who defeated him shows up. It is lighthearted and full of laughs.
77: Sgt. Frog by Mine Yoshizaki (Tokyopop) is a goofy sci-fi comedy. Sergeant Keroro is a frog-like alien sent to lead an invasion of Earth, but he ends up captured by the Hinata family. Now he lives with them, doing chores and building plastic model kits; his plans to conquer the planet keep failing spectacularly. Fans of parody and slapstick humor will love it.
78: Spice and Wolf by Isuna Hasekura and Keito Koume (Yen Press) is a manga adaptation of the beloved fantasy novels. Kraft Lawrence is a traveling merchant who finds a surprise in his wagon: Holo, a wolf goddess of the harvest in the form of a young woman. Holo wants to return to her northern home, so the two travel together. It is a rich, warm story full of witty banter and business deals.
79: Konosuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World! by Natsume Akatsuki and Masahito Watari (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy that pokes fun at the isekai genre. Kazuma Sato dies an embarrassing death and gets a chance to be reborn in a fantasy world. He decides to bring the snooty goddess Aqua along with him; he soon ends up leading a party of lovable but useless adventurers. It is silly fun.
80: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya by Nagaru Tanigawa (Yen Press) is a quirky school comedy with a sci-fi twist. Kyon is an ordinary high schooler whose new classmate, Haruhi Suzumiya, only cares about meeting aliens, time travelers, and espers. She drags him into forming a club, the SOS Brigade, to find them; what Haruhi does not realize is that strange things are already happening around her. It is clever, odd fun.
81: Project Arms by Kyoichi Nanatsuki and Ryoji Minagawa (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series. Ryo Takatsuki is a high schooler who lost his right arm as a child and had it replaced. One day, when danger strikes, he learns his arm is actually a powerful weapon made of nanomachines; he also meets other teens with similar arms, all targets of a mysterious organization. It is intense, fast-paced action.
82: A Centaur's Life by Kei Murayama (Seven Seas) is a gentle slice-of-life comedy. In this world, humans evolved with animal features, and Himeno Kimihara is a centaur, half girl and half horse. She is going through high school with her friends, dealing with homework, crushes, and quirky family; along the way, the series explores how this world works. It is cozy and funny.
83: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime by Fuse (Yen Press) is a feel-good fantasy adventure. Satoru Mikami, a 37-year-old office worker, is stabbed and dies, only to wake up in another world as a slime. He soon meets Veldora, a sealed dragon, and the two become friends; taking the name Rimuru, he begins helping the monsters around him and building a home for them. It is great for fans of kingdom-building stories.
84: Angel Sanctuary by Kaori Yuki (Viz Media) is a dark gothic fantasy drama. Setsuna Mudo is a troubled teen who harbors forbidden feelings for his sister, Sara; he learns that he is the reincarnation of Alexiel, an angel who rebelled against Heaven. Now both angels and demons want him, and Setsuna is dragged into a war between Heaven and Hell. It is dramatic and intense, best for older teens.
85: Hana-Kimi by Hisaya Nakajo (Viz Media) is a lively romantic comedy. Mizuki Ashiya is a Japanese American girl who admires high jumper Izumi Sano so much that she moves to Japan to be near him. There is just one problem: he goes to an all-boys high school; Mizuki disguises herself as a boy and enrolls, even ending up as his roommate. It is funny, sweet, and full of hijinks.
86: Cheeky Angel by Hiroyuki Nishimori (Viz Media) is a gender-bending school comedy with romance. As a young boy, Megumi asked a magical genie to become the manliest man around, but the genie had other ideas and turned him into a girl instead. Now a beautiful high schooler, Megumi still acts like a tough guy and gets into fights, much to her many admirers' confusion. It is fun and chaotic.
87: Pokémon Black and White by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is a kid-friendly adventure set in the Unova region. Black is a boy with a big dream of winning the Pokémon League; White runs a talent agency for Pokémon who perform in commercials and shows. When their paths cross, they team up and travel together, facing rival trainers along the way. It is a great fit for young Pokémon fans.
88: Classroom of the Elite by Syougo Kinugasa (Seven Seas) is a sharp school drama full of mind games. Kiyotaka Ayanokoji enrolls at Advanced Nurturing High School, an elite school where students are ranked by class and earn rewards for their performance. He is placed in Class D, home to the school's so-called rejects; to climb the rankings, the class must outwit their rivals. It suits readers who love strategy.
89: Trapped in a Dating Sim by Yomu Mishima (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action comedy. An ordinary man dies and is reborn as Leon Fou Bartfort, a minor noble inside a romance video game his sister made him play. In this world, women hold all the power, and men like Leon are background characters; using his knowledge of the game, Leon tries to secure a quiet life. It is funny and full of twists.
90: Ultraman by Eiichi Shimizu and Tomohiro Shimoguchi (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series that brings the classic hero into a new era. Shinjiro Hayata is a teenager who discovers he has strange powers; his father was the original Ultraman, who lost his memories of the role years ago. When alien threats return, Shinjiro is recruited to wear a new Ultraman suit. Fans of armored heroes will enjoy it.
91: Vampire Knight by Matsuri Hino (Viz Media) is a moody supernatural romance. Yuki Cross was rescued from a vampire attack as a child and now lives at Cross Academy, where a secret Night Class is made up of vampires. Yuki and her friend Zero Kiryu serve as guardians, keeping the human students from learning the truth. Meanwhile, Yuki is drawn to Kaname, the vampire who saved her life.
92: Kuma Kuma Kuma Bear by Kumanano (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. Yuna is a fifteen-year-old shut-in who spends her days playing an online game. One day she is pulled into the game world, wearing a fluffy bear costume that turns out to give her incredible powers; as she explores, she uses her strength to help people. It is cute, cozy, and fun.
93: xxxHolic by CLAMP is an eerie supernatural mystery from the creators of Cardcaptor Sakura. Kimihiro Watanuki can see spirits and is plagued by them; one day, he stumbles into a shop run by Yuko Ichihara, a mysterious woman who can grant any wish for a price. To pay for his wish to stop seeing spirits, he starts working for her. It is moody, stylish, and full of unsettling stories.
94: Yotsuba&! by Kiyohiko Azuma (ADV) is a joyful slice-of-life comedy. Yotsuba is an energetic, curious five-year-old girl who has just moved to a new town with her father. Everything is new and exciting to her, from swings to air conditioning, and she soon makes friends with the three sisters next door. It is a delight for readers of all ages.
95: Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead by Haro Aso and Kotaro Takata (Viz Media) is a lively horror comedy. Akira Tendo is worn out by his soul-crushing office job; when a zombie apocalypse breaks out in Tokyo, he realizes he never has to go to work again. Instead of despairing, he makes a list of one hundred things he wants to do before he becomes a zombie. It is bright, funny, and surprisingly uplifting.
97: Shugo Chara! by Peach-Pit (Kodansha) is a magical girl adventure about finding yourself. Amu Hinamori is seen as cool and spicy by her classmates, but inside she is shy and unsure. She wishes she could be braver, and the next morning she finds three eggs in her bed; each hatches into a little guardian character representing a different side of her. It is sweet, fun, and full of heart.
98: Yotsuba&! by Kiyohiko Azuma (Yen Press) is a joyful slice-of-life comedy. Yotsuba is an energetic, curious five-year-old girl who has just moved to a new town with her father. Everything is new and exciting to her, from swings to air conditioning; she soon makes friends with the three sisters next door; each chapter follows her small adventures. It is a delight for readers of all ages.
99: Basara by Yumi Tamura (Viz Media) is a sweeping post-apocalyptic adventure with romance. In a ruined future Japan ruled by a cruel royal family, a boy named Tatara was prophesied to be the child of destiny who will save the land. When Tatara is killed, his twin sister Sarasa takes his place and leads the rebellion in disguise. Readers who enjoy big quests and strong heroines will be swept away.
100: Missions of Love by Ema Toyama (Kodansha) is a shojo romance with a sharp, scheming edge. Yukina Himuro is a quiet, serious student who secretly writes hit cell-phone novels, though she has never been in love herself. When she discovers the secret of Shigure Kirisaki, the school's most popular boy, she blackmails him into helping her research romance one mission at a time. It's a fun pick for readers who like push-and-pull power games in their love stories.
101: Sword Art Online by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action light novel set inside virtual reality. When the new online game Sword Art Online launches, thousands of players log in and discover they can't log out, and dying in the game means dying for real. Kirito, a skilled solo player, sets out to clear all one hundred floors and free everyone. It's a great fit for gamers and anyone who enjoys high-stakes adventure with a touch of romance.
102: Takane and Hana by Yuki Shiwasu (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy built on a sharp-tongued rivalry. High schooler Hana Nonomura agrees to stand in for her older sister at an arranged marriage meeting with Takane Saibara, the arrogant heir to a huge corporation. Instead of being cowed, Hana tells him exactly what she thinks, and Takane finds himself fascinated. Readers who love bickering couples and quick-witted heroines will have a great time.
103: Grimgar of Fantasy and Ash by Ao Jyumonji (Seven Seas) is a grounded fantasy adventure light novel. Haruhiro wakes up in a strange world called Grimgar with no memories except his name, surrounded by other confused young people. To survive, they join the volunteer soldier corps and form a party, only to find that fighting even small goblins is hard, frightening work. It's a thoughtful read for fans who want a fantasy world where every victory is earned.
104: Baccano! by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is a mystery-action light novel full of gangsters, alchemists, and colorful crooks. In Prohibition-era America, a mysterious elixir of immortality sets off a chain of events that pulls mobsters, thieves, and bystanders into each other's paths. The story jumps between a big cast and several timelines, with plenty of humor along the way. Readers who enjoy clever, puzzle-like plots and stylish 1930s settings will want to dig in.
105: Bakuman by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a shonen drama about two teens chasing their dream of making manga. Moritaka Mashiro is a talented artist who has given up on his dream until his classmate Akito Takagi, a gifted writer, asks him to team up. Together they set out to create a hit series for Weekly Shonen Jump. It's a fascinating look inside the manga industry for anyone who loves comics or creative work.
106: How a Realist Hero Rebuilt the Kingdom by Dojyomaru (Seven Seas) is a fantasy light novel about running a country instead of fighting monsters. Kazuya Souma is summoned to another world to be a hero, but he offers the king a plan for fixing the kingdom's economy instead. Impressed, the king hands him the throne and engages him to his daughter. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy politics, strategy, and smart problem-solving in their fantasy.
107: In/Spectre by Kyo Shirodaira (Kodansha) is a supernatural mystery with a playful, clever streak. As a child, Kotoko Iwanaga was taken by spirits and became their goddess of wisdom, settling disputes among yokai and ghosts. Now in college, she sets her sights on Kuro Sakuragawa, a young man whom even the spirits fear, and together they solve strange cases where the truth matters less than a convincing explanation. Fans of puzzle-box mysteries and folklore will enjoy it.
108: Kakegurui by Homura Kawamoto (Yen Press) is a psychological thriller set in a school ruled by gambling. At elite Hyakkaou Private Academy, students' rank depends on how much they win, and losers become the school's servants. Then Yumeko Jabami transfers in, a sweet-seeming girl who loves risky bets more than winning itself. It's a tense, stylish read for anyone who enjoys mind games and over-the-top high stakes.
109: Kare First Love by Kaho Miyasaka (Viz Media) is a shojo romance and drama about a first relationship. Karin Karino is a shy, plain high schooler who doesn't think anyone would notice her, until Kiriya Aikawa, a handsome boy from another school, spots her and becomes interested, and Karin has to figure out what she wants as she navigates her first love. It's a sweet, honest read for fans of classic school romances.
111: Reincarnated as a Sword by Yuu Tanaka (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action light novel with an unusual hero. A man dies and is reborn in another world, not as a person but as a magic sword stuck in the ground. When he meets Fran, a young cat-girl escaping a cruel life, he becomes her weapon and protector as they set out to grow stronger together. Readers who enjoy found-family bonds and leveling-up adventures will like it.
112: Maison Ikkoku by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a gentle romantic comedy set in a run-down boarding house. Yusaku Godai is a struggling student who can never study thanks to his noisy, nosy neighbors. Just as he decides to move out, the house gets a new manager, Kyoko Otonashi, a young widow he falls for at first sight. It's a warm, funny classic for readers who like slow-burn love stories and lovable eccentric casts.
113: Shikimori's Not Just a Cutie by Keigo Maki (Kodansha) is a sweet romantic comedy about a couple who are already together. Izumi is a kind but very unlucky high schooler, and his girlfriend Shikimori is adorable and loving. But whenever trouble comes his way, Shikimori turns unbelievably cool and swoops in to save him. It's a cozy, feel-good read for anyone who enjoys wholesome couples and lighthearted school life.
114: Ooku: The Inner Chambers by Fumi Yoshinaga (Viz Media) is a historical drama set in an alternate Edo-era Japan. A mysterious disease kills most of the country's young men, and women step into the roles of farmers, merchants, and even shogun. The shogun's inner chambers are now filled with handsome men who serve her. It's a rich, thoughtful story about power and gender, perfect for readers who love history and complex characters.
115: 07-Ghost by Yuki Amemiya and Yukino Ichihara (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy adventure. Teito Klein is a former slave studying at a military academy in the Barsburg Empire, haunted by lost memories. After he uncovers a terrible secret, he flees and takes shelter in a church, where he meets bishops who seem to know more about his past than he does. Fans of gothic fantasy, magic battles, and mysterious pasts will enjoy it.
116: Neon Genesis Evangelion by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action story about giant machines and the people inside them. Fourteen-year-old Shinji Ikari is summoned to Tokyo-3 by the father he barely knows, who orders him to pilot a giant bio-machine called an Evangelion. His job is to fight the mysterious Angels attacking the city. It's an intense, emotional read for fans of mecha and character-driven science fiction.
117: Banana Fish by Akimi Yoshida (Viz Media) is a crime drama set in 1980s New York. Ash Lynx is a brilliant young gang leader who keeps hearing the words "banana fish," a phrase tied to his brother's breakdown in Vietnam. When he meets Eiji Okumura, a kind Japanese photographer's assistant, the two are pulled into a dangerous conspiracy. It's a gripping, emotional read for anyone who loves gritty thrillers and deep friendships.
119: The Irregular at Magic High School by Tsutomu Sato (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action light novel set in a world where magic is a science. Siblings Tatsuya and Miyuki Shiba enroll at First High School for magicians. Miyuki is a top student, while Tatsuya is placed among the lower-ranked students, even though his real abilities are anything but ordinary. Readers who like detailed magic systems and quietly overpowered heroes will feel right at home.
120: O-Parts Hunter by Seishi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a shonen action adventure. Ruby is a treasure hunter searching for O-Parts, ancient artifacts that grant powers to people with the right spirit energy. Along the way, she meets Jio, a hot-tempered boy who wants to take over the world and can use O-Parts himself, and the two team up. It's a good fit for fans of fast fights, ancient relics, and big-hearted heroes.
121: The Rising of the Shield Hero by Aneko Yusagi (One Peace Books) is a fantasy action light novel about an underdog hero. Naofumi Iwatani is summoned to another world as one of four legendary heroes, but he gets the Shield Hero role, which can't attack. Soon after, he is betrayed and falsely accused, leaving him alone and mistrusted. Readers who enjoy redemption arcs and heroes who earn their strength the hard way will be hooked.
122: I'm Standing on a Million Lives by Naoki Yamakawa (Kodansha) is a fantasy action story with a game-like twist. Yusuke Yotsuya is a detached high schooler who is suddenly pulled into another world along with two classmates. They are given quests to clear, and while they can come back after dying, failing a quest could have real consequences, and Yusuke's assigned class is a lowly farmer. It's a fun pick for fans of strategic isekai stories.
123: D-Frag! by Tomoya Haruno (Seven Seas) is a goofy shonen comedy about a school club gone wild. Kenji Kazama thinks of himself as a tough delinquent, but after a run-in with the members of the Game Creation Club, he finds himself forced to join. The club's girls are eccentric, explosive, and never take no for an answer. It's a great pick for readers who want fast, silly gags and a lovable cast.
124: Knights of the Zodiac by Masami Kurumada (Viz Media) is a classic action fantasy, also known as Saint Seiya. Seiya is a young orphan trained to become a Saint, a warrior who wears armor based on the constellations. After winning his Pegasus Cloth, he and his fellow Saints are drawn into battles to protect the goddess Athena. It's a great fit for fans of old-school shonen battles, mythology, and friendship.
125: Witch Hat Atelier by Kamome Shirahama (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure full of wonder. Coco has always dreamed of being a witch, but everyone knows witches are born, not made. When she secretly watches a witch named Qifrey cast a spell, she learns magic is drawn, and her first try goes terribly wrong, so she becomes Qifrey's apprentice. The detailed, beautiful art makes it a favorite for fantasy readers of all ages.
126: Something's Wrong With Us by Natsumi Ando (Kodansha) is a romance and suspense story set in the world of traditional Japanese sweets. Nao is a talented young confectioner whose mother was accused of a crime years ago. When she meets Tsubaki, the heir to a famous sweets shop, she realizes he is connected to her past and enters his family's home to uncover the truth. It's a tense, stylish read for fans of dramatic mysteries.
127: Splatoon by Sankichi Hinodeya (Viz Media) is a colorful kids action comedy based on the Nintendo game. In the city of Inkopolis, squidlike Inklings battle in Turf War, a team sport where the goal is to cover the most ground in ink. Goggles and his teammates are always ready to jump into a match. It's a bright, funny read for young gamers and anyone who loves the Splatoon series.
129: An Archdemon's Dilemma: How to Love Your Elf Bride by Fuminori Teshima (J-Novel Club) is a sweet fantasy romance light novel. Zagan is a feared sorcerer with a bad reputation and no idea how to talk to people. When he spends his fortune at an auction to free a beautiful elf named Nephy, he suddenly has to figure out how to live with her. It's a cozy, awkward-in-the-best-way read for fans of gentle romance.
130: Strike the Blood by Gakuto Mikumo (Yen Press) is a supernatural action light novel. Kojou Akatsuki is an ordinary high schooler on Itogami Island, except that he's secretly the Fourth Primogenitor, the world's most powerful vampire. A young sword shaman named Yukina Himeragi is sent to watch him and stop him if he becomes a threat. It's a good fit for fans of vampires, magic battles, and school-life comedy.
131: Fist of the North Star by Buronson and Tetsuo Hara (Viz Media) is a classic action story set after a nuclear war. In a ruined world ruled by gangs and warlords, the wanderer Kenshiro uses Hokuto Shinken, a deadly martial art that strikes the body's pressure points. He fights to protect the weak and find the woman he loves. It's a great pick for fans of martial arts and gritty, larger-than-life heroes.
132: The Apothecary Diaries by Natsu Hyuuga (Square Enix) is a historical mystery set in an imperial court. Maomao, a young woman trained as an apothecary, is kidnapped and sold as a servant to the emperor's rear palace. She plans to keep her head down, but her curiosity gets the better of her when the emperor's children fall ill, and soon the handsome eunuch Jinshi notices her talents. It's a clever read for mystery and palace-drama fans.
133: Anonymous Noise by Ryoko Fukuyama (Viz Media) is a shojo romance and drama about music and first love. Nino Arisugawa loves to sing, and as a child she was close to two boys, Momo and Yuzu, who both left her life; years later, she keeps singing in hope that her voice will reach them. When the three cross paths again in high school, everything gets complicated. It's a great pick for fans of band stories and love triangles.
134: Ascendance of a Bookworm by Miya Kazuki (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy drama about a girl's love of books. A college student who adores reading dies and is reborn as Myne, a sickly little girl in a world where books are rare and only the rich can afford them. Determined to read again, she sets out to make books herself, starting from nothing. It's a charming, thoughtful read for anyone who loves books and clever heroines.
135: Battle Royale by Koushun Takami and Masayuki Taguchi (Yen Press) is a dark thriller based on Takami's novel. Shuya Nanahara and his classmates think they're going on a school trip. Instead, they wake up on an island and learn they've been chosen for a government program that forces them to fight until only one is left. It's a tense, violent story best suited to older readers who enjoy survival thrillers.
136: The King's Beast by Rei Toma (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance with revenge at its heart. Rangetsu is an Ajin, part human and part beast, whose twin brother was killed while serving in the royal palace. To find out who did it, she disguises herself as a boy and becomes a servant to Prince Tenyou, but she starts to have feelings for him. It's a great fit for fans of palace intrigue and slow-burn romance.
137: Goong by Park So-hee (Yen Press) is a romance and drama manhwa set in a modern Korea that still has a royal family. Chae-kyung is an ordinary, outspoken high school girl who learns that her grandfather promised her in marriage to the crown prince. Before she knows it, she's engaged to Shin, a cold and distant prince. It's a fun read for anyone who enjoys royal romance and fish-out-of-water comedy.
138: Otomen by Aya Kanno (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy that flips expectations. Asuka Masamune is a kendo champion and the picture of a tough, manly guy, but secretly he loves cooking, sewing, and all things cute. He hides his hobbies, until he falls for Ryo, a girl who is great at martial arts but hopeless at domestic tasks. It's a funny, kind-hearted read for anyone who loves warm romance and great gags.
140: Priest by Hyung Min-woo (Tokyopop) is a dark horror and action manhwa set in the American Old West. Ivan Isaacs was once a priest, but after a tragedy he made a deal with a demon, gaining terrible power in exchange for his soul. Now he hunts down a fallen angel and his undead followers across the frontier. It's a gritty, stylish pick for fans of horror westerns and bold, dramatic art.
141: Dark Gathering by Kenichi Kondo (Viz Media) is a shonen horror story about ghost hunting. Keitaro Gentoga is a college student who attracts spirits, and a past encounter left him wary of the supernatural. Then he becomes a tutor for Yayoi Hozuki, a brilliant young girl who collects dangerous spirits in hopes of finding the one that took her mother. It's a creepy, exciting read for fans of spooky action and Japanese ghost stories.
142: Witchcraft Works by Ryu Mizunagi (Vertical) is a fantasy action comedy about a boy with an unexpected protector. Honoka Takamiya is an ordinary high schooler until he learns that Ayaka Kagari, the school's beautiful, untouchable princess, is a powerful witch. She's sworn to protect him, because Honoka has something inside him that other witches want. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy role-reversal and magical battles.
143: Didn't I Say to Make My Abilities Average in the Next Life?! by FUNA (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy light novel. A girl who was always too talented for her own good dies and asks to be reborn with average abilities. She is reborn as Adele, and she gets the average of every creature in the world, which makes her absurdly powerful, and as she tries to live a normal life as an adventurer, chaos follows. It's lighthearted fun for isekai fans.
144: Say I Love You by Kanae Hazuki (Kodansha) is a shojo romance and drama. Mei Tachibana has kept to herself for years, after being hurt by friends in the past. When the popular Yamato Kurosawa accidentally gets kicked by Mei, he becomes interested in her, and soon announces she's his friend, and Mei must learn to trust people again. It's a heartfelt read for fans of slower, emotional love stories.
145: Dr. Slump by Akira Toriyama (Viz Media) is a zany comedy from the creator of Dragon Ball. In the strange little town of Penguin Village, eccentric inventor Senbei Norimaki builds a robot girl named Arale, who is super strong but doesn't know how anything works, which leads to lots of chaos. It's packed with silly gags and wild characters, perfect for younger readers and fans of Toriyama's playful humor.
147: Drifting Dragons by Taku Kuwabara (Kodansha) is a seinen fantasy adventure about life aboard a dragon-hunting airship. The crew of the Quin Zaza sails the skies hunting dragons for their meat, oil, and other valuable parts. Mika, a young hunter who loves the thrill and the food, is at the center of the action. It's a fun, mouth-watering read for anyone who loves adventure stories with a cooking twist.
148: Magical Girl Raising Project by Asari Endou (Yen Press) is a dark, psychological magical girl light novel. A popular mobile game secretly turns some of its players into real magical girls, but soon the game announces that there are too many of them, and half must be eliminated. Koyuki, who just wants to be a hero, is pulled into a deadly competition. It's a tense, gritty read for fans who like their magical girls with an edge.
149: Mars by Fuyumi Soryo (Kodansha) is a shojo romance and drama. Kira is a shy, quiet art student who has trouble connecting with people. Rei is a charming but reckless playboy who races motorcycles, and after Kira lets him see her sketchbook, an unlikely bond forms between them. It's a moving, mature read for fans of emotional love stories with deep, flawed characters.
150: Medaka Kuroiwa Is Impervious to My Charms by Ran Kuze (Kodansha) is a shonen romantic comedy. Mona Kawai is the most popular girl in school, and no boy has ever resisted her charms, until Medaka Kuroiwa, a monk-in-training who has sworn off romance and won't give her a second look, so Mona makes it her mission to win him over. It's a sweet, silly read for fans of playful will-they-won't-they comedy.
151: Failure Frame by Kaoru Shinozaki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy action light novel. Touka Mimori is summoned to another world with his classmates, but he is ranked as the weakest. The goddess who summoned them throws him into a deadly ruin to die, but Touka survives, uncovers his real abilities, and sets out to get revenge. It's a fit for readers who enjoy darker isekai stories with clever, unconventional heroes.
153: The 100 Girlfriends Who Really, Really, Really, Really, Really Love You by Rikito Nakamura (Seven Seas) is a wildly silly romantic comedy. Rentaro Aijo has been rejected one hundred times, and he wishes for love at a shrine. The god of love tells him he will meet one hundred soulmates, and if he doesn't love them all, they'll be in danger. It's a fast, absurd, and big-hearted read for fans of over-the-top comedy.
154: A Condition Called Love by Megumi Morino (Kodansha) is a shojo romance about learning what love feels like. Hotaru Hinase has never really understood love, but one day she does a kind deed for Hananoi, a handsome boy, and he suddenly asks her to date him. As she spends time with him, she slowly starts to figure out her own feelings. It's a gentle read for fans of cute, heartfelt school romances.
155: Baby & Me by Marimo Ragawa (Viz Media) is a heartwarming shojo comedy and drama. After his mother dies, ten-year-old Takuya Enoki has to help take care of his baby brother, Minoru, while their dad works. It's not always easy for a kid to balance school and friends with caring for a toddler. It's a sweet, gently funny story for anyone who loves family-centered stories with plenty of heart.
156: Nina the Starry Bride by RIKACHI (Kodansha) is a shojo fantasy romance. Nina is an orphan girl who survives on the streets, until Prince Azure notices her blue eyes and wants her to pose as a princess who has died, so she can be married off in her place, and as Nina learns to live in the palace, she and Azure grow closer. It's a lovely read for fans of royal romance and beautiful art.
157: Mob Psycho 100 by ONE (Dark Horse) is a shonen action comedy from the creator of One-Punch Man. Shigeo Kageyama, nicknamed Mob, is a quiet middle schooler with enormous psychic powers. He tries to keep his emotions in check, since his powers can go wild if he loses control, and he works for a fake psychic named Reigen. It's funny, heartfelt, and full of surprises.
158: Ajin: Demi-Human by Gamon Sakurai (Vertical) is a seinen action thriller about an immortal on the run. High schooler Kei Nagai is hit by a truck and killed, then comes back to life, which makes him an Ajin, a rare kind of human who can't die, and the government wants to capture and experiment on him. It's a tense, smart read for fans of sci-fi thrillers.
159: My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected by Wataru Watari (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy light novel with a sharp, cynical voice. Hachiman Hikigaya is a loner who thinks youth is a lie. After he turns in an essay complaining about it, his teacher forces him to join the Service Club, run by the cool and brilliant Yukino Yukinoshita. It's a witty read for fans of complex characters and realistic school drama.
160: The Royal Tutor by Higasa Akai (Yen Press) is a comedy set in the royal court of a European-style kingdom. Heine Wittgenstein is hired to tutor the four princes of Granzreich, each of whom is a handful. The serious, small-statured tutor must find a way to help each prince grow, in the hope that one will become king. It's a fun, heartfelt read for fans of court life and found family.
161: I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years and Maxed Out My Level by Kisetsu Morita (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy comedy. After working herself to death in an office job, Azusa is reborn as an immortal witch and chooses a quiet life in the countryside. She spends three hundred years killing slimes every day and, without realizing it, reaches the maximum level, and soon visitors start showing up. It's a relaxing read for fans of slow-life fantasy.
162: Bofuri: I Don't Want to Get Hurt, so I'll Max Out My Defense. by Yuumikan (Yen Press) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy light novel. Kaede Honjo starts playing a virtual reality game and decides she doesn't want to get hurt, so she puts all her points into defense. Playing as Maple, she ends up nearly impossible to beat, in hilarious ways. It's a fun, cheerful read for gamers and anyone who loves comfort-food fantasy.
163: Inubaka: Crazy for Dogs by Yukiya Sakuragi (Viz Media) is a seinen comedy for dog lovers. Suguri Miyauchi is a young woman with a special way with dogs who lands a job at a pet shop, where she gets to meet dogs of all breeds, and their often quirky owners. Each chapter mixes comedy with useful tidbits about dog care and breeds. It's a fun, easygoing read for anyone who loves dogs.
165: Requiem of the Rose King by Aya Kanno (Viz Media) is a historical drama inspired by Shakespeare's Richard III. In England during the Wars of the Roses, young Richard of York grows up in a world of war, betrayal, and family rivalry. Richard hides a secret about his body that his own mother calls a curse. It's a dark, dramatic read for fans of Shakespeare and gothic historical stories.
166: La Corda d'Oro by Yuki Kure (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance about music. Kahoko Hino is a general education student at a school known for music, and she has never played an instrument, until she meets a tiny fairy named Lili, who gives her a magic violin and enters her in the school's music competition, where Kahoko has to learn to play from the heart. It's a great pick for music and romance fans.
167: Laid-Back Camp by Afro (Yen Press) is a cozy slice-of-life comedy about camping. Rin Shima loves to camp on her own near Mount Fuji, and one day she meets Nadeshiko Kagamihara, a cheerful girl who is new to the area and has fallen asleep by a lake. Rin shares her campsite, and Nadeshiko catches the camping bug. It's a relaxing, warm read for anyone who loves the outdoors and good food.
168: Dengeki Daisy by Kyousuke Motomi (Viz Media) is a shojo romance and mystery. When Teru Kurebayashi's brother dies, he leaves her a cell phone and tells her to contact a mysterious person named Daisy when she needs help, and Daisy becomes her secret support. Meanwhile, she ends up working for Kurosaki, a rude school janitor. It's a fun mix of romance, comedy, and suspense for fans of slow-burn relationships.
169: When Will Ayumu Make His Move? by Souichirou Yamamoto (Kodansha) is a sweet romantic comedy. Ayumu Tanaka is a quiet high schooler in the shogi club who has a crush on his senior, Urushi Yaotome. He has decided he won't confess until he beats her at shogi, which seems hard to do, and meanwhile the two flirt in their own way. It's from the creator of Teasing Master Takagi-san, and fans of cute couples will love it.
170: LDK by Ayu Watanabe (Kodansha) is a shojo romance about two teens who end up living together. Aoi Nishimori lives on her own and doesn't have much interest in dating until the school's most popular boy, Shusei Kugayama, moves in next door, and after a mishap, he ends up moving into her apartment, and she starts to see a different side of him. It's a fun, swoony read for fans of shojo romance.
171: Love Com by Aya Nakahara (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy. Risa Koizumi is the tallest girl in her class, and Atsushi Otani is the shortest boy, and they fight so much that people call them a comedy duo. When Risa realizes she's falling for him, she has to figure out how to win his heart. It's a funny, heartwarming read for fans of bickering couples.
172: She Professed Herself Pupil of the Wise Man by Ryusen Hirotsugu (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Kagami Sakimori plays a VR game as Danblf, a wise, elderly sage. When he changes his avatar to a young girl, he suddenly finds himself trapped in the game world, which has become real, and to avoid embarrassment, he claims to be the sage's pupil, Mira. It's a fun read for fans of gaming isekai stories.
173: Soul Eater: The Perfect Edition by Atsushi Ohkubo (Square Enix) is a shonen action story about students who train to become weapons and meisters. At Death Weapon Meister Academy, Maka Albarn and her partner Soul Eater, who can transform into a scythe, hunt evil souls. Their goal is to make Soul into Death's own weapon. It's a stylish, high-energy read for fans of supernatural action.
174: By the Grace of the Gods by Roy (J-Novel Club) is a cozy fantasy light novel. Ryoma Takebayashi is an overworked man who dies and is reborn in another world as a young boy, blessed by the gods. Living in the forest, he spends his days taming slimes and studying them before he ventures out to meet people and start a business. It's a relaxing read for fans of gentle isekai and slow-life stories.
175: Wandering Witch: The Journey of Elaina by Jougi Shiraishi (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel. Elaina is a young witch who sets out to travel the world, as in the stories she loved as a child. She visits all kinds of countries and meets all kinds of people, each with their own story, some happy and some sad. It's a thoughtful read for fans of travel stories and anthology-style fantasy.
177: Gabriel Dropout by Ukami (Yen Press) is a comedy about angels and demons at school on Earth. Gabriel White Tenma was the top student at angel school, sent to Earth to learn about humans. But she discovers online games and turns into a lazy shut-in, while her friends, including angels and demons, try to help, or make things worse. It's a silly, lighthearted read for fans of slice-of-life comedy.
178: Akashic Records of Bastard Magic Instructor by Taro Hitsuji (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action comedy. Glenn Radars is a lazy man who gets a job as an instructor at a magic academy, and he doesn't seem to care at all, but when the school is in danger, Glenn shows his skills and courage, and serious student Sistine soon realizes he's more than he seems. It's a fun read for fans of magic schools and unlikely heroes.
179: The Asterisk War by Yuu Miyazaki (Yen Press) is an action romance set in a city of combat schools. Ayato Amagiri transfers to Seidoukan Academy in Asterisk, where students fight in tournaments to win their wishes. On his first day, he accidentally sees Princess Julis changing, and she challenges him to a duel. It's a fun pick for fans of school battles and fantasy action.
180: The Demon Prince of Momochi House by Aya Shouoto (Viz Media) is a shojo supernatural romance. On her sixteenth birthday, orphan Himari Momochi inherits a house that sits on the border between the human and spirit worlds. When she arrives, she finds three handsome young men already living there, including Aoi, the house's guardian. It's a beautiful, atmospheric read for fans of yokai and romance.
182: Hitorijime My Hero by Memeco Arii (Kodansha) is a boys' love romance. Masahiro Setagawa is a teen who has gotten mixed up with a bad crowd when he is saved by a tough guy named Kousuke Ooshiba, who turns out to be his new math teacher at school, and as they spend more time together, feelings start to grow. It's a sweet, emotional read for fans of BL romance and found family.
183: The New Gate by Yoshiyuki Miwa (One Peace Books) is a fantasy adventure. Shin is a player trapped in a deadly VR game, and he finally defeats the final boss to set everyone free, but instead of waking up at home, he finds himself back in the game world, five hundred years later. It's a good fit for fans of gaming isekai stories with strong heroes.
184: Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World by Kei Sazane (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance light novel. Iska is a young swordsman from the empire, which has been at war for years with the nation of witches, and on the battlefield he faces Aliceliese, a powerful witch princess; though enemies, they begin to respect each other. It's a great pick for fans of star-crossed romance and big battles.
185: Parasyte by Hitoshi Iwaaki (Kodansha) is a classic horror and sci-fi story. Alien parasites arrive on Earth and take over human brains, turning their hosts into monsters, and when one tries to take over high schooler Shinichi Izumi, it fails and ends up in his right hand instead. Now Shinichi and the parasite, Migi, must work together to survive. It's a gripping read for fans of body horror and thoughtful science fiction.
186: Peach Boy Riverside by Coolkyousinnjya (Kodansha) is a fantasy action story inspired by the folktale of Momotaro. Princess Sally has lived a sheltered life in her castle, and she wants to see the world, and when she meets Mikoto, a boy who hunts oni, she learns the world is more dangerous than she thought as she sets off on a journey of her own. It's a good fit for fans of folklore-inspired adventures.
187: In Another World With My Smartphone by Patora Fuyuhara (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Touya Mochizuki dies by accident, and God feels so bad that he sends Touya to a new world, letting him bring one thing along, so he chooses his smartphone. With it and new magical skills, Touya sets off on fun adventures. It's a lighthearted read for fans of easygoing isekai stories.
188: Persona 5 by Hisato Murasaki (Viz Media) is a supernatural action story based on the popular video game. Ren Amamiya is a high schooler on probation who transfers to a new school in Tokyo, and when he finds a strange app on his phone, he is pulled into the Metaverse, a world shaped by people's hearts, where he and his friends become the Phantom Thieves. It's a fun pick for gamers and fans of stylish action.
190: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel. Bell Cranel is a young adventurer in the city of Orario, where adventurers explore a huge dungeon for treasure. He is the only member of the Hestia Familia, led by the goddess Hestia, and after a powerful swordswoman saves him, Bell wants to become strong. It's a great fit for fans of classic dungeon-crawling fantasy.
191: Cherry Magic! Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?! by Yuu Toyota (Square Enix) is a boys' love romantic comedy. Kiyoshi Adachi is a shy office worker who turns thirty and finds he can read people's minds by touching them, and he learns that his handsome, popular coworker Kurosawa has a crush on him. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of workplace romance and gentle BL.
192: Pokemon Adventures by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is a kids adventure series based on the Pokemon games. Red is a boy who dreams of becoming a great Pokemon trainer, and with his Pokemon by his side, he travels the region, battling trainers and facing off against Team Rocket. It's a fun pick for young fans who love the games.
193: Psyren by Toshiaki Iwashiro (Viz Media) is a shonen sci-fi action story. High schooler Ageha Yoshina finds a strange red phone card and makes a call, and he is transported to a ruined world called Psyren, filled with monsters, where to survive, he must find out what Psyren is and why he's been brought there. It's a gripping read for fans of mystery and superpowered battles.
195: Real by Takehiko Inoue (Viz Media) is a seinen sports drama about wheelchair basketball. Kiyoharu Togawa, a former track star who lost his leg, plays wheelchair basketball with a fierce passion. Tomomi Nomiya is a high school dropout who feels guilty after a crash, and their stories explore struggle and hope. It's from the creator of Slam Dunk, and it's a powerful read for sports and drama fans.
196: Video Girl Ai by Masakazu Katsura (Viz Media) is a shonen romance with a sci-fi twist. Yota Moteuchi is a lovesick high schooler who has just been rejected, and when he rents a video from a strange shop, and a girl named Ai steps out of the screen to cheer him up, though Ai isn't quite what he expected. It's a classic, sweet, and emotional read for fans of 90s romance.
197: W Juliet by Emura (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy. Ito Miura is a tomboy in her school's drama club, and a beautiful new transfer student named Makoto turns out to be a boy, who must pass as a girl through high school to prove to his father he can be an actor, and Ito promises to keep his secret. It's a fun read for fans of romance and disguise comedies.
198: Konosuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World! by Natsume Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel. Kazuma Sato dies in an embarrassing way and is given a choice to be reborn in a fantasy world, and he decides to bring the goddess Aqua with him, who turns out to be useless, before their party grows with more odd members. It's a hilarious read for fans of fantasy parody.
199: Rozen Maiden by PEACH-PIT (Seven Seas) is a supernatural drama. Jun Sakurada is a shut-in boy who hasn't been to school in a while, until he receives a strange box, which holds a living doll named Shinku, who makes him her servant and drags him into a battle between dolls. It's a gothic, emotional read for fans of beautiful art and character-driven stories.
200: Saint Seiya: Saintia Sho by Chimaki Kuori (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action story set in the world of Saint Seiya. Shoko is an ordinary, hot-headed girl until her older sister Kyoko is taken by the goddess Eris. To get her back, Shoko joins the Saintia, the female warriors sworn to guard the goddess Athena. It's a good pick for fans of the original series and anyone who likes armored heroines and big battles.
201: Wolf Girl and Black Prince by Ayuko Hatta (Viz Media) is a high school romantic comedy built on one small lie. Erika Shinohara wants to fit in with her friends, so she claims to have a boyfriend and backs it up with a photo of a handsome stranger. When he turns out to be Kyoya Sata from her own school, he agrees to play along, on the condition that she becomes his loyal "dog." Readers who like prickly, push-and-pull romances will feel at home.
203: Yamada-kun and the Seven Witches by Miki Yoshikawa (Kodansha) is a school romantic comedy with a supernatural twist. Ryu Yamada is a delinquent with bad grades and no friends, until he tumbles down the stairs with Urara Shiraishi, the top student in school, and the two wake up in each other's bodies. Their swap leads them into the school's secret of the seven witches. It's lively and funny, with a mystery thread running underneath.
204: Magical Girl Apocalypse by Kentaro Sato (Seven Seas) is a horror action story that turns magical girls into a nightmare. Kii Kogami is a shy high school otaku who would rather be left alone. Then one ordinary school day, murderous magical girls appear and start slaughtering everyone in sight, leaving Kii and a handful of classmates fighting to survive. Expect fast pacing and plenty of gore, so it's best for readers who like intense survival horror.
205: Magical Girl Site by Kentaro Sato (Seven Seas) is a dark psychological horror story. Aya Asagiri is bullied at school and miserable at home, and she has started to wish she could just disappear. Then a strange website called the Magical Girl Site appears on her screen and hands her a "stick" with real power, pulling her into a deadly world of other magical girls. It's grim and violent, best for fans of dark takes on the genre.
206: Your Lie in April by Naoshi Arakawa (Kodansha) is a drama about music, grief, and first love. Kosei Arima was a child piano prodigy until his mother's death left him unable to hear his own playing. Now in middle school, he has given up music, until he meets Kaori Miyazono, a free-spirited violinist who drags him back toward the stage. It's heartfelt and bittersweet, a good pick for readers who like emotional stories with real warmth.
207: Malevolent Spirits: Mononogatari by Onigunsou (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action story about the spirits that live inside old objects. Hyoma Kunato is a young exorcist with a deep grudge against tsukumogami. He is sent to Kyoto to live with Botan Ise, a girl who shares her home with a whole family of them, and living under one roof forces him to rethink what he believes. It mixes stylish battles with found-family warmth.
209: So I'm a Spider, So What? by Okina Baba (Yen Press) is a fantasy light novel series with a very unusual hero. After a mysterious explosion wipes out her high school class, one girl is reborn in another world as a tiny spider monster at the bottom of a dungeon full of creatures that want to eat her. Her upbeat inner voice keeps the survival story funny, and fans of offbeat isekai and game-style leveling will have a great time.
210: So I'm a Spider, So What? by Okina Baba (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure adapted from the light novel series, with art by Asahiro Kakashi. After a mysterious explosion wipes out her high school class, one girl is reborn in another world as a tiny spider monster, stranded deep in a dungeon full of hungry monsters.
